payload.headline: Tesla holds near 383.72 while sales stall and cash flow shrinks; still avoid

summary.thesis: Tesla's price assumes strong growth, but sales were flat last quarter and operating margin and free cash flow both fell, so the stock trades near the top of its own valuation range.
summary.decision: Long-term the call is avoid, and there is no swing trade until the price breaks out of its 364.02–396.23 range or the 2027-01-27 report arrives.
summary.act_at: Reconsider near 293.94; swing only on a close above 396.23 or below 364.02

payload.happening: Tesla closed at 383.72, up 0.95% on the day. That puts it inside the 380.15–388.56 zone, just under resistance at 389.95–396.23. There is no news since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
payload.business: Three things in DATA change the business itself. Sales stopped growing. Revenue in the latest quarter was -0.17% versus a year earlier, compared with 15.78% two quarters ago. Profitability fell. Operating margin, the share of each sales dollar left after running costs, dropped to 3.35% from 4.74%. Cash generation weakened too: trailing free cash flow, the cash left after spending on the business, fell to 3.3B from 6.8B. The filings show two more warning signs. Inventory rose 15% while sales were flat, and unsold cars can force price cuts. Each invested dollar now earns 5¢ a year, down from 33¢ three years ago. Survival is not at risk. Tesla holds 37.5B of net cash, meaning cash minus debt, and 45.4B of total liquidity against 8.0B of debt. The real risk is to margins and to the growth story that supports the price. The macro view of a tech downtrend with elevated fear affects sentiment, not the business.

worth.text: The methods disagree sharply. A discounted cash flow model (DCF), which values a company on the cash it is expected to produce, gives 19.87 in the bear case, 24.41 in the base case and 43.62 in the bull case. Even at 30% starting growth, it reaches only 44.18. Those values are low because the starting cash base is only 3.3B of free cash flow and the discount rate is 10.1%. A second method compares the price with Tesla's own past price-to-sales ratios, meaning price divided by yearly revenue. On that basis, value runs from 203.8 at the low end through 293.94 in the middle to 399.81 at the high end. Today's 14.6 times sales sits at the 73rd percentile of Tesla's own 5-year history. Trailing earnings are 422.2 times, on a market value of 1517.0B. According to the filings, the price needs about 52% yearly growth, while Tesla has delivered 3% a year over 3 years. The gap between the methods comes down to one question: does the market keep paying for future growth, or does it start paying for today's cash?
worth.key_assumption: The market keeps valuing Tesla within its own 5-year price-to-sales range rather than on its current 3.3B of free cash flow.

bull: The balance sheet is strong: 37.5B of net cash and 45.4B of liquidity pay for heavy spending without new borrowing.
Trailing revenue still grew 8.3%, to 103.6B from 95.6B.
The valuation inputs include analysts' next-year EPS growth of 25%. If that is delivered, the cash base behind the valuation would rise.
bear: The price is 422.2 times trailing earnings, while even the bull DCF case is only 43.62 per share.
Operating margin fell to 3.35% from 4.74%, and free cash flow halved to 3.3B from 6.8B.
Inventory rose 15% while latest-quarter sales were flat at -0.17%, which raises the risk of price cuts.

levels.what: Today's close. It sits near the top of the own-history range and far above the DCF base of 24.41.
The top of the own-history price-to-sales range. Above it, even the most generous method calls the stock expensive.
The middle of the own-history range. Re-examine there if operating margin stops falling below 3.35%.

longterm.why: Sales have stalled and margins and cash flow are shrinking, yet the price assumes a high multiple. The business is graded D and the committee call is Reduce.

swing.why: The trend is a downtrend, and the 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (386.13, 375.81 and 382.08) are all flat. Support at 364.02–368.6 and resistance at 389.95–396.23 are both close relative to the 15.63 average daily range, so a stop would sit inside normal noise. A close above 396.23 or below 364.02 would show a direction.

decision.timing: No new position before the 2027-01-27 report, the next real test of margins and cash flow. Options price a 4.8% move by 2026-11-20, 12.0% by 2026-12-18 and 19.6% by 2027-02-19, so swings within the range before then are noise.

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74% and quarterly revenue growth back toward the 15.78% of two quarters ago.
Trailing free cash flow climbs back toward 6.8B from 3.3B, which would lift the DCF cash base.
The price falls to 293.94, the middle of the own-history range, while net cash holds near 37.5B.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still avoid and no trade, because the price, now 383.72, remains stuck below resistance at 389.95–396.23 with no new news and no change in the shrinking margin and cash-flow figures.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
